title: Eat the Rainbow! Colorful Fruits and Veggies for Kids with Pip
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Pip the strawberry, and this is my buddy Kiko the broccoli!
Welcome to Fruity Friends! Today we're meeting a rainbow of foods.
Can you count with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Healthy food and healthy habits help us grow big and strong.
Ready? Let's go to the kitchen!

lines: Here's a clue: it's round and crunchy, and it can be red, green or yellow! Can you guess?
This is Apple! Can you say apple?
Crunch, crunch! Apples are fun to bite.
Can you pretend to pick an apple from a tree? Reach up high!
Little seeds! They make a star shape.
One more time, nice and loud: APPLE!
Apples help keep your teeth and tummy happy.
Here's a clue: it's orange and crunchy, and it grows under the ground! Can you guess?
This is Carrot! Can you say carrot?
Carrots grow down in the dirt.
The green leaves stay on top, and the carrot hides below!
Can you pull a carrot out of the ground? Pull, pull, POP!
No! Some are purple, yellow or white.
One more time, nice and loud: CARROT!
Carrots help your eyes stay healthy.
Here's a clue: it's yellow, and it has lots of little bumps in rows! Can you guess?
This is Corn! Can you say corn?
Each yellow bump is a kernel.
Can you grow tall like a corn plant? Stretch, stretch!
What are the yellow bumps called?
Kernels! Lots and lots of kernels.
One more time, nice and loud: CORN!
Corn is sweet and sunny yellow.
Here's a clue: it looks like a tiny green tree! Can you guess?
This is Broccoli! Can you say broccoli?
Each little bump is called a floret.
Can you stand tall like a broccoli tree? Arms up!
Little trees! You can be a giant!
One more time, nice and loud: BROCCOLI!
Broccoli helps you grow big and strong.
Here's a clue: they're tiny, round and blue! Can you guess?
This is Blueberries! Can you say blueberries?
They are small, so you can eat a handful!
Can you count three blueberries on your fingers? One, two, three!
Blue! Well, a little bit purple, too.
One more time, nice and loud: BLUEBERRIES!
Blueberries are tiny but very good for you.

outro: Which one was your favorite? Tell a grown-up, and try something new this week!
Bye, friends! See you next time on Fruity Friends!
